about:
# Dyre's Buff Reminders

Your class buffs, each in its own icon, cast with one click, with a red
border when one drops, also in combat; ammo and reagent counts; a Paladin seal
timer; cooldown chimes; and proc arcs and sounds. For World of Warcraft: Forever. Settings are in **Options → AddOns → Dyre's
AddOns → Buff Reminders**, or type `/dbr`. They are saved per character.

- **Druid: Thorns follows your tank.** With a member set to the Tank role,
  Thorns watches that tank and a click casts it on them. Solo, with no tank,
  as the tank yourself, or when the tank is dead, offline, or out of range,
  it watches you.
- **Hunter: Aspect reminder and aspect bar.** A red outline when there is
  an aspect problem: no aspect up, or a fight with Cheetah or Pack up
  (Speed-Running mode allows Cheetah). One click puts your last combat
  aspect up, with an optional sound at combat start. An aspect bar swaps
  aspects with one click and shows which one is up.
- **Warrior: Battle Shout, Overpower, and Revenge.** A Battle Shout
  reminder, and a sound the moment Overpower or Revenge
  becomes usable, also in combat. A Hunter gets the same for Mongoose Bite.
- **Ammo for any bow, gun, or crossbow** (Hunters, Warriors, and Rogues): the
  count, red and pulsing when low, and a reminder to equip your ammo when
  none is equipped. It counts in combat too.
- **Each buff its own icon**, always shown, in a place you choose that never
  moves: the buff with its time left while it is up, a red border you click
  to cast when it is missing, yellow and flashing before it runs out, moved
  and sized with Dyre's Toolkit.
- **Also in combat:** if a buff on you expires, is dispelled, or is
  cancelled, its red reminder shows at once, and a click recasts it.
- **Reagents:** Rebirth's seeds (Druid), Arcane Powder (Mage), Infernal
  Stones and Demonic Figurines (Warlock), counted with the ammo.
- Hidden on flight paths; each icon shows the spell a click casts.
- In combat AddOns cannot read buffs, so group members' buffs (and Thorns on
  the tank) are checked again after the fight; the seal timer, the combat
  aspect icon, the ammo and reagent counts, the chimes, and the procs
  keep working.

## Buff reminders

An icon for each of your class buffs, with a border that tells you where it
stands: a glow or a red border while it is missing (**Missing buff**: Glow,
the action bars' proc glow, or Red border), yellow and flashing while it is
about to run out, none while it is up. Each buff has its own icon in its own place,
which never moves on its own; one you do not know or have switched off shows
nothing. They start in two rows: buffs that can go on another player above,
your own below.

- **Always shown.** While the buff is on you, the game draws it in its place
  with its time left, in and out of combat alike, so nothing appears or
  disappears when a fight starts or ends.
- **When it is missing** (expired, dispelled, or cancelled) the reminder
  shows there at once with its glow or red border, also in combat, and a click recasts it on
  you. In combat the game itself hides the buff's icon (AddOns cannot read
  buffs then), so the reminder underneath shows through.
- **Out of combat** the reminder also shows while anyone in your group lacks
  the buff, or yours is about to run out (with a countdown), with the smart
  click (group members, the tank, the group version). That stays as it is
  through a fight; your group is checked again after it.
- Unlocked, every icon shows (the buffs that are on, dimmed).
- **Show only when needed**, a switch under each buff (on at first for
  Battle Shout, off for long buffs: with it on, a buff dispelled or
  cancelled in a fight shows only at its warning time or after the fight,
  as AddOns cannot see it go then; off, it shows at once): while
  the buff is up, its icon and the game's buff icon in its place show at
  **Visibility when not needed** (0%, hidden, at first; up to 80%), the same
  in and out of combat, until **Remind before a buff runs out** (or a buff's
  own time); then it shows in full with the yellow flashing border. A
  missing buff always shows in full with its glow or red border. Off, the icon
  always shows in full. In combat AddOns cannot read buffs, so DBR times
  them from the last read and your own casts: a buff that drops early in a
  fight (dispelled or cancelled) shows at its warning time, and a group
  member who lacked it before the fight keeps it in full. A hidden icon
  still takes clicks in combat: a click on its place casts the buff.
- **Show only in combat**, a switch under Battle Shout, beneath **Show only
  when needed** (off at first): on, Battle Shout shows nothing out of combat
  (no icon, no buff icon, no flashing border), also when it is missing or
  about to run out. In combat it shows as before.

| Class | Buffs |
|---|---|
| Mage | **Arcane Intellect** (also for group members who use mana), **Armor** (Frost, Ice, or Mage Armor), **Dampen or Amplify Magic** (off at first; either counts, a click recasts the last one) |
| Warlock | In a group where you aren't the tank, a message on screen while the Voidwalker's Torment or Suffering is on autocast (with Dyre's Threat and Combat Tools installed, it gives this warning instead, and DBR stays quiet); **Demon Armor** (Demon Skin counts before you learn it); **Pet (your demon)**: red while you have no demon, also in combat, and a click summons the last demon you summoned, else the Imp (not after a Demonic Sacrifice, nor while mounted) |
| Warrior | **Battle Shout** (it reaches your party; watched on you). Shown only when needed (its own switch): missing, or in its last 60 seconds (its own **Remind before it runs out**, 5-120 s), out of combat and in it (in combat timed from your own casts); it needs rage, which runs out soon after a fight |
| Hunter | In a group where you aren't the tank, a message on screen while your pet's Growl is on autocast (with Dyre's Threat and Combat Tools installed, it gives this warning instead, and DBR stays quiet). **Aspect**: a red outline only when there is a problem (no aspect up; in a fight, Cheetah or Pack up), in Normal, Speed-Running, or Disabled mode; a click recasts the last combat aspect you cast (Hawk, Monkey, Viper, Wild, or Beast), never Cheetah or Pack, else Hawk, else Monkey; **Pet**: red while you have no pet or it is dead, also in combat (not while mounted); a click calls it, or revives it when it is dead, and a right-click revives it |
| Druid | **Mark of the Wild** (also for your group), **Thorns** (on your group's tank, else on you) |
| Priest | **Power Word: Fortitude** (also for your group), **Inner Fire**, and as options **Divine Spirit** (group members who use mana) and **Shadow Protection** (your group) |
| Paladin | **Righteous Fury** (on you; solo, or as your group's tank: the Tank role, or a raid's main tank; or with **Always show Righteous Fury** switched on; blessings are left to AddOns such as PallyPower). In a group where you aren't the tank, a message on screen while it is on. And the seal timer below |

Coming from Mage Tools Forever or Warlock Tools Forever? On DBR's first run
on a character it copies that AddOn's reminder settings (which are on, the
group switch, and your last armor) once; icon places start fresh.

- Every rank counts, and only buffs you know show. Rogues and Shamans
  have no reminders yet; DBR says so once at login and
  shows nothing.
- For group buffs, the icon shows how many lack the buff, and its tooltip
  who. Dead, offline, or out-of-sight members are skipped. Each group buff
  has a switch to remind you only about yourself.
- **Click an icon to cast the buff.** It goes to you first, then to the next
  group member in range who lacks it, so each click moves down the list. With
  two or more missing, it casts the group version instead (Arcane Brilliance,
  Gift of the Wild, Prayer of Fortitude, Prayer of Spirit, or Prayer of Shadow
  Protection) if you know it and carry its reagent.
- **Before it runs out:** a share of the buff's own length before it ends,
  its border turns yellow and flashes, so you can recast it in time: 10% at
  first, so 3 minutes before a 30-minute buff ends and 1 minute before a
  10-minute one. **Remind before a buff runs out** sets the share (0-20%; 0
  warns only once it is gone). Out of combat the icon also shows a
  countdown of the time left, and group members' buffs count too. In combat
  the yellow border comes from when your buff runs out, as DBR last read it,
  and your own recast resets it (a single-target cast counts when it went on
  you: no friendly target, or yourself targeted). Battle Shout keeps its own
  time in seconds.
- Your armor icon recasts the one you used last, else your best.
- **Hunters: the Aspect reminder.** It shows only when there is a
  problem, with a red outline and your last combat aspect (else Hawk, else
  Monkey): no aspect up, in or out of combat, or a fight with Aspect of the
  Cheetah or the Pack up. Cheetah or Pack out of combat is travel, so
  nothing shows. **Aspect** under **Reminders** picks the mode: **Normal**
  (default), **Speed-Running** (Cheetah is fine in a fight, for killing
  fast in the open world; no aspect or Pack still shows it), or
  **Disabled**. A click casts your last combat aspect with "!", so it never
  takes an aspect down. It is set up before the fight (AddOns cannot change
  it during one). In a fight, a click on it or on an aspect bar button
  hides it at once; a combat aspect cast from your action bar dims it and
  takes the outline away (it never turns invisible). If you cancel an
  aspect during a fight, it shows when the fight ends. An optional sound
  plays when a fight starts with a problem (its own switch and choice).
  **Aspect reminder: size** (50-200%) and **opacity** size it.
- **Thorns follows the tank.** In a party or raid with a member in the Tank
  role, Thorns watches that tank, and a click casts it on them (with several,
  the first in group order who is alive, online, in sight, and in range).
  Solo, with no tank, as the tank yourself, or with the tank dead, offline,
  or out of range, it watches you, and a click casts it on you.
  The tooltip says whom. Whom a click casts on is set before a fight and
  stays through it: group and role changes apply after it; a tank who dies
  or moves out of range mid-fight makes the game refuse the cast, and if
  someone joins or leaves mid-fight the click can reach whoever takes the
  tank's party slot. While the tank has Thorns, its icon shows the tank's
  time left (the game's icon in its place shows only your own buffs); in a
  fight AddOns cannot see the tank's buffs, so it turns yellow before and
  red when it runs out by the time DBR read before the fight, and a dispel
  on the tank shows only after it. Recasting it on the tank while you
  target them restarts that time.
- **Druids in Bear, Cat, or another form:** a click leaves the form and casts
  the buff. It cannot put you back in your form: the game lets only your own
  key press cast, and changing form has to wait for the global cooldown.
- The game does not let AddOns read buffs in combat, so your group's buffs
  are checked again after a fight. The icons hide on a flight path, and come
  back when you land.

## Aspect bar (Hunters)

A bar with a button for each aspect you know: Hawk, Monkey, Viper (where the
game has it), Beast, Wild, Cheetah, and Pack, in that order. Click one to
swap to that aspect. A click never turns an aspect off, so clicking the one
that is up does nothing. The aspect that is up has a gold border; in combat
the border follows the aspects you cast, because the game does not let
AddOns read buffs then. An aspect or rank you learn in combat shows after
the fight. The bar hides while you are dead or on a flight path and shows
while mounted.

It is on at first. **Enable** under **Aspect bar** in `/dbr` turns it off; **Layout** (Horizontal or Vertical; **Vertical** with a Dyre's Toolkit before 2.18.0) lays the buttons out in a row or a column, and **Aspect bar:
size** and **opacity** size it. It sits under your buff icons at first; move
it with `/dbr unlock`. A click on an aspect bar button in a fight also
hides or shows the Aspect reminder.

## Seal timer (Paladins)

While a seal is up, its icon shows with the time left counting down, and a
bar under it, also in combat. In combat with no seal up, your last seal
shows with the pulsing gold border and a full gold bar under it; click it to
cast that seal. Out of
combat with no seal up, nothing shows. Every seal counts, Forever's Seal of Fury
and any other seal in your spellbook included. **Seal timer**
turns it off.

## Ammo and reagents

Hunters, Warriors, and Rogues: with a bow, crossbow, or gun in your ranged slot, the
**Consumables** bar shows your equipped arrows or bullets and how many are
left, also in combat. At or below **Warn at** (200 at first) the count turns
red and pulses; out of ammo it shows as missing. With none equipped it shows
as missing too, and its tooltip says to equip the ones in your bags. Thrown
weapons and wands take no ammo, so they show nothing. **Enable** and
**Ammo** under **Consumables** in `/dbr` turn it off.

Mages: once you know Arcane Brilliance, the bar counts your Arcane Powder
(**Warn at** 5 at first, 0-40). Warlocks: Infernal Stones once you know
Inferno and Demonic Figurines once you know Ritual of Doom (**Warn at** 1
each at first, 0-10).

Druids: once you know Rebirth, the same bar counts the seeds your highest
rank uses (Maple, Stranglethorn, Ashwood, Hornbeam, or Ironwood Seed), also in
combat. At or below its own **Warn at** (2 at first, 0-10) the count turns
red and pulses; with none left it shows as missing. Gift of the Wild's Wild
Berries or Wild Thornroot count the same way once you know it (**Warn at** 5
at first). **Rebirth reagent** under **Consumables** turns it off; a new
rank or spell shows its setting after a `/reload`.

Classes with nothing to count (for now Priests, Paladins, and Shamans), and
characters who do not know a reagent spell yet, have no Consumables
settings.

## Moving the icons

DBR needs **Dyre's Toolkit** 2.0 or later (the CurseForge app installs it
with DBR). Without it, DBR stays off and says once at login where to get it.

`/dbr unlock` (or `/dyre unlock`, or **Unlock frames** on the Dyre's AddOns
page) unlocks every Dyre's AddOn at once: each buff icon, the ammo bar, and
the seal timer show their outline. Drag each where you like; it snaps to
the other Dyre's frames (Shift-drag moves a snapped row together) and, if
you choose, to the toolkit's grid. `/dbr lock` locks them again and
`/dbr reset` puts them back in their default places. Each thing's size
(50-200%) and opacity, with **Reset size**, sit at the end of its own
section on DBR's settings page: **Reminder icons** (every buff icon) and
the seal timer at the end of **Reminders**, the Consumables bar at the end
of **Consumables**.

## Profile (copy, export, import)

With Dyre's Toolkit 2.10.0 or newer, DBR's settings are part of your
character's **Dyre's Toolkit profile**, with every other Dyre's AddOn. On
the Toolkit's settings page (its **Profile** section) you can copy every
setting from another character, or the Defaults, and export or import them
as one line of text. A copy applies at once, with no reload, and never in
combat. Copied: the switches, sounds, leads, the frames' places, sizes, and
opacity. Not copied (each character keeps its own): the spell each button
casts last, the cooldown lengths and buff IDs DBR read in game, and the
debug probe. A copy from another class is fine: DBR keeps a setting for
every class's buffs. With an older Toolkit, nothing changes.

## Cooldown chimes

A sound just before your chosen spells are ready again, so you can act the
moment they are, also in combat. Every class has a list (a Mage's Blink,
Frost Nova, and Counterspell; a Warlock's Death Coil; a Druid's Barkskin; and
so on).

- **Every rank counts.** A spell is matched by its name. Blizzard's Cooldown
  Manager on Forever treats each rank as a different spell; the chimes do
  not.
- Each spell has its own switch and its own sound, side by side on one row
  (with an older Dyre's Sounds, the sound sits under the switch); choosing a
  sound plays it. Text to Speech says "Blink ready".
  **Chime early** moves every chime 0-3 seconds before the cooldown ends
  (default half a second). **Enable** under **Chimes** turns them all off.
- The game hides cooldowns from AddOns in combat, so DBR times each one from
  your cast: the length it last read, else Forever's. A spell
  you cast in a fight (such as Counterspell) is read when the fight ends, if
  its cooldown still runs, so the next chime uses its real length. Cold Snap
  and Preparation cancel the chimes of the spells they reset.
- **The sounds come from Dyre's Sounds.** Install it from CurseForge (the
  CurseForge app installs it with DBR). Without it, the chimes play nothing,
  DBR says so once at login, and the buff reminders work as usual.
- Your chime settings carry over on the first run: from Dyre's Cooldown
  Chimes if you used it, else from Mage Tools Forever or Warlock Tools
  Forever. Dyre's Cooldown Chimes is now part of DBR: remove its folder;
  while it is installed, it plays the chimes and DBR plays none.

## Procs

An arc each side of your character while a proc is up, and a sound the
moment it appears, so you can use it, also in combat. Each proc has its own
arc switch, sound switch, and sound. The arcs and their art come from Dyre's
Shields Up, which now shows only shields (1.13.0); this needs Dyre's Toolkit
2.12 or later.

| Class | Procs |
|---|---|
| Mage | **Missile Barrage** and **Fingers of Frost** (both arcs and sound); **Clearcasting** (Arcane Concentration): sound only, off at first (the game already plays one) |
| Warlock | **Nightfall** (Shadow Trance: arcs on, sound off at first) and **Decimation** |
| Druid | **Clearcasting** (Omen of Clarity): arcs on, sound off at first; **Nature's Grace**: sound only at first |
| Shaman | **Clearcasting** (Elemental Focus): arcs on, sound off at first |
| Hunter | **Mongoose Bite** (after your target dodges): arcs while usable (dimmed while you lack the mana) and a sound the moment it becomes usable, once you know it |
| Warrior | **Overpower** and **Revenge**: arcs while usable (dimmed while you lack the rage) and a sound the moment one becomes usable (any sound; at most once per 3 seconds each); **Flurry**: off at first |

- A proc shows only when you know its talent. Fingers of Frost's right arc
  goes when you use one of its two charges.
- The Missile Barrage tooltip has a macro that catches it, also during a
  cast, with Arcane Missiles in your client's language.
- The game plays a buff proc's sound itself, because AddOns cannot read
  your buffs in combat; only sounds the game can play for a buff are listed.
  During a boss encounter a change you make applies after it.
- DBR starts from Classic's spell IDs and checks them in game: the first
  time a proc's buff is on you out of combat (for example right after a
  fight), DBR reads its real ID and uses it from then on.
- **Proc arc size** sets how big the arcs are; `/dbr unlock` moves them.
- Once, on the first login with this version, DBR copies your proc choices
  from Dyre's Shields Up (arcs, sounds, the arcs' place and size) and keeps
  its own Proc Chimes sounds where you had set them. Chat says so.
- With SpellActivationOverlay loaded, DBR's arcs stay off and the sounds
  still play; turn on **Show proc arcs with SpellActivationOverlay** to show
  both (after a `/reload`).
- With a Dyre's Toolkit older than 2.12, DBR keeps 1.12's **Proc Chimes**:
  the sounds only, with one **Enable** switch.
- On a Warlock, your Nightfall sound setting carries over from Warlock Tools
  Forever on the first run. With an older Warlock Tools Forever still
  playing it, DBR says so once at login.

## Cast chimes

A sound just after you cast a travel spell or shift into a Druid form, also
in combat: every cast chime waits 0.2 seconds, just after the game's own
spell sound starts. Druid: shifting into **Travel Form** ("Meep meep"), **Bear** or
**Dire Bear Form** ("Rawr"), **Cat Form** ("Meow"), **Aquatic Form**
("Splash"), or **Moonkin Form** ("Hoot hoot"), 0.2 seconds after you shift
and only if you are still in that form (powershifting chimes once), never
when you leave a form;
**Dash** (off at first). Hunter: **Aspect of the Cheetah** (on) and **Aspect
of the Pack** (off at first). Rogue: **Sprint** (on). Warrior: **Charge**, **Intercept**, and **Execute** (on);
**Whirlwind**, **Battle Shout**, **Demoralizing**, **Challenging**, and
**Intimidating Shout**, **Taunt**, and **Rend** (off at first); on
Anniversary also **Intervene**, **Commanding Shout**, and **Victory Rush**,
once known. Druid, in Bear Form: **Feral Charge** (once you have the
talent) and **Enrage** (on), **Demoralizing** and **Challenging Roar**,
**Bash**, and **Frenzied Regeneration** (off at first). The Warrior's and
these play Dyre's Sounds 1.2.0's "Dyre's Aggression"
sounds at first (an older Dyre's Sounds plays its default chime). Every rank counts. At
first Text to Speech says those words ("Meep meep" for the travel spells)
(set up a voice under the game's Text to Speech options; without one, the
chimes' default sound plays); choose any Dyre's Sounds sound per spell under
**Cast Chimes** in `/dbr`, whose **Enable** turns them all off. Sprint and
Dash also have a cooldown chime under **Chimes**; Travel Form and the
aspects have no cooldown.

## Combo point chimes

Rogues, and Druids in Cat Form: a note as you earn each combo point, rising
from low Bb, a held note when you reach the most, and low Bb again when you
spend them, also in combat. Several points at once play in order. One point
fading out of combat, a new target, and leaving Cat Form are silent. Under
**Combo Point Chimes** in `/dbr`: **Enable**, **Full** and **Spend** (each
with its own sound), **Only when full**, and **Note set**:

- **Bassoon** (the default; Dyre's Sounds 1.4.0's "Dyre's Bassoon"): a quick
  comic climb, the held F at the most.
- **Sax** (Dyre's Sounds 1.3.0's "Dyre's Sax"): a scale up to the held high
  Bb.
- **Same as Full**: each point plays the Full sound.

Full and Spend follow the set unless you chose your own sound. With a Dyre's
Sounds older than 1.4.0 the Bassoon plays the Sax notes; with one older than
1.3.0, its default chime.

## With Mage Tools Forever or Warlock Tools Forever

Mage Tools Forever (from 1.2.0) and Warlock Tools Forever (from 1.3.0) rely
on Dyre's Buff Reminders for their buff reminders and cooldown chimes, and
install it with them. The first time DBR runs on a character, it copies that
AddOn's reminder settings once (see above). An older MTF or WTF may still
show its own reminders or play its own chimes; DBR says so once at login, and
you can turn them off in MTF or WTF.

With Dyre's Toolkit 2.17.0 or later, MTF and WTF can show DBR's settings for
your class on their own pages: the buff reminders, the cooldown chimes, and
the procs. They are the same settings as on DBR's page, so a change on one
page is the change on the other.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/dbr`, `/dbr options` | Opens the settings (out of combat): Reminders, Aspect bar (Hunters), Consumables, Chimes, Procs, and Cast Chimes |
| `/dbr unlock`, `/dbr lock` | Unlocks every Dyre's AddOn's frames to drag them, and locks them again |
| `/dbr reset` | Moves the buff icons, the aspect bar, the Consumables bar, and the seal timer back to their default places |
| `/dbr debug` | Diagnostics: each reminder, who lacks it, what a click casts, and any spell IDs the client does not know; the seal timer; each chime spell, Dyre's Sounds, and the latest chime events; and each proc, its spell IDs, and whether it is confirmed in game |
| `/dbr probe on`, `/dbr probe off` | A test aid: chat lines when a Warrior's, Rogue's, or Hunter's reactive abilities (Overpower, Revenge, Execute, Riposte, Mongoose Bite, Counterattack) become usable or glow; off by default |

`/buffreminders` works the same, in case another AddOn uses `/dbr`.

## Compatibility

For World of Warcraft: Forever 1.60.1 (tested on build 70450, Interface
16001). It also loads on Classic Era (Interface 11509). If a client update
removes an API it needs, it says so in chat and
stays off.

**Verified in client:** the Paladin seal timer, with Seal of Fury, and
Righteous Fury; Druid Mark of the Wild, Thorns, and the Rebirth seed count;
the Hunter aspects; the always-shown buffs and recasting in combat; the proc
sounds on a Warlock (Nightfall) and a Warrior's Revenge.

**Not yet verified in client:** the Priest buffs, the group versions' spell
IDs and reagents, the Mage and Warlock reagents, and the chime lists of
classes other than Mage and Warlock; the proc arcs in DBR (1.13.0), which
were checked in Dyre's Shields Up. [TESTING.md](https://github.com/jbedworth/DyresBuffReminders/blob/main/TESTING.md) has the
checklist.

WowUp users (2.24.0 or later): install from the repository URL; GitHub releases
carry the Forever metadata WowUp needs.

## Support

Dyre's AddOns are free. If you enjoy them, you can support them on Ko-fi: https://ko-fi.com/dyre_janelle

# Dyre's Buff Reminders 1.16.0

## Changes

### Features

- The Aspect bar can now have one opacity out of combat and another in combat, like every Dyre's button bar. While your mouse is over it, it shows at 80% or more, so you can always see what you click. Both start at the opacity you have now. This needs Dyre's Toolkit 2.19 or later. Its two sliders take the old Opacity slider's place, so you see opacity there only once.

## Notes

- For WoW: Forever and WoW Classic Era. Built for Forever beta 1.60.1,
  build 70450, Interface 16001, and Classic Era 1.15.9,
  build 70003, Interface 11509. DBR runs on later builds
  while the client provides the APIs it needs, and says so in chat if they are missing.
- Buff reminders for Mages, Warlocks, Druids, Priests, and Paladins: a pulsing
  icon for each class buff missing on you or your group, or about to run out,
  out of combat. Click it to cast the buff. Paladins also get a seal timer.
- Cooldown chimes for every class: a sound just before your chosen spells are
  ready again, also in combat, and proc arcs and sounds (Clearcasting,
  Nightfall, and so on). The sounds come from Dyre's Sounds.
- Settings in Options > AddOns, or `/dbr`; `/dbr unlock` to move the icons.

# Dyre's Buff Reminders 1.15.1

## Changes

### Fixes

- A cooldown chime for a spell you haven't learned yet is now greyed out on the Chimes page, its name and checkbox included, so it no longer looks like you can turn it on. You see the same on Warlock Tools Forever's and Mage Tools Forever's Chimes pages. Learn the spell and its row lights up. Your choices for it stay as you set them.

## Notes

- For WoW: Forever and WoW Classic Era. Built for Forever beta 1.60.1,
  build 70450, Interface 16001, and Classic Era 1.15.9,
  build 70003, Interface 11509. DBR runs on later builds
  while the client provides the APIs it needs, and says so in chat if they are missing.
- Buff reminders for Mages, Warlocks, Druids, Priests, and Paladins: a pulsing

# Dyre's Buff Reminders 1.14.0

## Changes

### Features

- **Your Buff Reminders settings on Mage Tools Forever's and Warlock Tools Forever's pages.** With Dyre's Toolkit 2.17.0 or later, those AddOns can show DBR's own switches for your class on their settings pages: the Reminders, the Chimes, and the Procs, all of your class's. They are the same settings as on DBR's page: a change on one page is the change on the other. Sizes, the aspect bar, consumables, and the cast and combo point chimes stay on DBR's page. With an older toolkit or class AddOn, nothing changes: those pages keep their button that opens DBR's page. Where the class AddOn supports it, each section's switch (**Reminders**, **Chimes**, **Procs**) can sit on the class AddOn's top page, and the rest on its sub-page, greyed while that Enable is off.

- **Procs: one switch for every proc arc and sound.** With Dyre's Toolkit 2.17.0 or later, the Procs section starts with **Enable**: off, every proc arc and sound stops; each proc's own switches keep their choices for when you turn it on again. On a class AddOn's top page it is named **Procs**. Every proc of your class is listed, greyed until you learn its talent.

### Fixes

- **One name for each section**: Reminders, Chimes, and Procs, the same on DBR's page and on the class AddOns' pages. The proc sounds section ("Proc Chimes") is now **Procs**.
- **Pet taunt warning only once**: with Dyre's Threat and Combat Tools installed, Hunters and Warlocks got the pet taunt warning twice, from it and from DBR. DBR now stays quiet whenever another Dyre's AddOn gives that warning, and its switch is greyed out, naming that AddOn. In layout mode, DBR's empty "Warning messages" frame no longer shows while it has no warning to give, and its sample shows your class's own warning (a Paladin's Righteous Fury), not always the pet taunt.
- **Shorter setting tooltips**: each one now says in one plain sentence what the setting does. The details are in the README.
- **Settings under a switch that is off are now greyed, all the way down.** Before, with Reminders' Enable off, the buffs were greyed but the rows under them (such as "also your group" and "Show only when needed") stayed bright. The sizes are greyed with their feature off too.

# Dyre's Buff Reminders 1.13.4

## Changes

### Features

- Hunter: **Mongoose Bite** is now a proc cue, as a Warrior's Overpower and Revenge: arcs while it is usable after your target dodges (dimmed while you lack the mana), and a sound the moment it becomes usable. On by default, once you know the spell. With a Dyre's Toolkit before 2.12, the sound only.
- Warrior: **Show only in combat**, a new switch under Battle Shout, just beneath **Show only when needed**. On, Battle Shout shows nothing out of combat, also when it is missing or about to run out; in combat it shows as before. Off by default.

### Fixes

- **Cooldown chimes for spells you cast only in combat** (such as Counterspell) no longer come early. DBR could read a cooldown only after a cast out of combat, so these spells kept DBR's built-in length. Counterspell's was wrong (24 seconds; it is 30 in Classic and on Forever), so it chimed about 6 seconds early. Now DBR reads a cooldown that is still running when combat ends, learns its real length, and moves the chime to it.
- **Cooldown chime lengths** now match Forever: Counterspell 30 seconds, Fear Ward 3 minutes, Lay on Hands 20 minutes, Holy Shock 10 seconds, Shield Wall 15 minutes, Last Stand 3 minutes, Retaliation 15 minutes, Freezing Trap 30 seconds, Multi-Shot 6 seconds, Stormstrike 8 seconds.
- Warrior: the **Death Wish** chime now follows Death Wish. Before, it followed Sweeping Strikes, so a Sweeping Strikes cast played "Death Wish ready".
- Shaman: the chime for Elemental Mastery is now named **Lightning Mastery**, Forever's name. Your setting stays.
- **Joining a group**: the pet taunt and Righteous Fury warnings, the Righteous Fury reminder for the tank, and the Thorns tank choice now check again 2 seconds after a group, role, or zone change. Before, the game could give its group, role, or pet bar data after the first check, and the warning stayed silent until something else changed.
